description: Indexes built with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY after the migrations, one statement at a time outside any transaction, so building them never blocks writes to a live table. For each, in order: drop it if it exists but is invalid (a build killed midway), build it if missing, then drop the index it replaces, so the table is never without one of them.

indexes.name: idx_runnerq_dequeue_effective_v2
indexes.doc: Single-type dequeue: with activity_type pinned by equality the rest of the key is the dequeue ORDER BY, so the claim is an index walk stopping at the first unlocked row.
indexes.sql:
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_runnerq_dequeue_effective_v2
ON runnerq_activities (
    queue_name,
    activity_type,
    priority DESC,
    retry_count DESC,
    COALESCE(scheduled_at, created_at) ASC
)
WHERE status IN ('pending', 'scheduled', 'retrying', 'waiting')

indexes.name: idx_runnerq_dequeue_order_v2
indexes.doc: Untyped and multi-type dequeue: key order is the dequeue ORDER BY, so Postgres never sorts the eligible backlog to find the top row.
indexes.sql:
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_runnerq_dequeue_order_v2
ON runnerq_activities (
    queue_name,
    priority DESC,
    retry_count DESC,
    COALESCE(scheduled_at, created_at) ASC
)
WHERE status IN ('pending', 'scheduled', 'retrying', 'waiting')

indexes.name: idx_runnerq_query_created
indexes.doc: QueryStorage: cross-queue, newest first; with a filter no other index serves (completed activities, a type), Postgres walks it and filters. The id tiebreaker matches the keyset cursor.
indexes.sql:
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_runnerq_query_created
ON runnerq_activities (created_at DESC, id DESC)

indexes.name: idx_runnerq_query_status
indexes.doc: QueryStorage by status, newest first, for every status but completed: live work and failures, the lists and counts the console polls. Completed, the bulk of the table, is left out so a completion writes no entry; its lists read idx_runnerq_query_created. Queries must name the statuses as literals so Postgres can prove the predicate.
indexes.sql:
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_runnerq_query_status
ON runnerq_activities (status, created_at DESC, id DESC)
WHERE status <> 'completed'

indexes.name: idx_runnerq_processing
indexes.doc: The reaper's scan of a queue's in-flight activities, which fleet concurrency bounds; it checks the lease on the row. Leaving lease_deadline_ms out of the key lets lease renewals update in place (HOT).
indexes.sql:
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_runnerq_processing
ON runnerq_activities (queue_name)
WHERE status = 'processing'

indexes.name: idx_runnerq_root_children
indexes.doc: A workflow's descendants. Roots are found by id, so they aren't indexed here: a tree is id = root OR (root_activity_id = root AND parent_activity_id IS NOT NULL).
indexes.sql:
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_runnerq_root_children
ON runnerq_activities (root_activity_id)
WHERE parent_activity_id IS NOT NULL

indexes.name: idx_runnerq_root_terminal
indexes.doc: Retention: a queue's finished roots by status, oldest first, so finding the oldest expired root is one short seek per terminal status. Each root gets one entry, when it finishes.
indexes.sql:
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_runnerq_root_terminal
ON runnerq_activities (queue_name, status, completed_at)
WHERE parent_activity_id IS NULL
  AND status IN ('completed', 'failed', 'dead_letter', 'cancelled')

indexes.name: idx_runnerq_results_by_owner
indexes.doc: An activity's checkpoints and signal results: its step history, and what deleting its tree removes.
indexes.sql:
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_runnerq_results_by_owner
ON runnerq_results (owner_activity_id)
WHERE owner_activity_id IS NOT NULL
